# rtl-sdr

> RTL2832U DVB-T dongle repurposed as a wideband receive-only SDR

**Vendor:** various (Realtek RTL2832U reference design)

Status: **supported** — the identifiers and setup recipe are believed correct.

**Not maintainer-verified**: nobody on this project has run this hardware yet. The two facts are recorded separately on purpose (D-027) — a correct recipe and a tested device are different claims.

## What it is

A television tuner dongle whose chipset can be driven as a general-purpose receiver, roughly 24 MHz to 1.7 GHz depending on the tuner, receive only. The cheapest way into SDR by a wide margin, and the reason most people have one.

## What you can do with it

Listen to broadcast and amateur bands, decode ADS-B, ISM-band sensors, POCSAG and AIS, and feed the whole utility-decoder cluster.

## Setup

Install the packages and add yourself to plugdev. Debian's rtl-sdr package ships udev rules and a modprobe blacklist for dvb_usb_rtl28xxu; without that blacklist the DVB driver claims the device first and rtl_test reports it as busy.

## Known problems

The dvb_usb_rtl28xxu kernel driver claiming the device is the single most common failure and looks like broken hardware. Clones vary enormously in oscillator stability — the `kalibrate-rtl` tool exists for exactly this, though it is not carried in this catalog yet. The librtlsdr rules file matches over forty rebadged devices, so a dongle sold under another name usually still works.

Group membership required: `plugdev` — added at install, applies at next login.
